clauses.why: An administrative enable/disable switch is beyond the request; access can be withheld without a dedicated kill switch.
Resuming submissions only exists because the spec introduced an enable/disable switch.
Visibility of the enablement state depends on the spec-introduced enable/disable switch.
A rollback capability for the activation is not called for by a request to create the bot.
A configuration inspection view is an added operator capability the request's purpose does not require.
Starting disabled presupposes the spec-introduced enablement switch.
An in-product disclosure notice is not required for a bot plainly requested as a Grok bot in a development org.
An eight-category failure taxonomy with subcategories goes well beyond reporting that a request failed.
Deduplicating duplicate deliveries of one attempt adds idempotency machinery beyond a basic question-and-answer bot.
Server-side expiry of attempt validity windows is added machinery the request does not call for.
Preserving deliberate retries only matters because the spec added duplicate-attempt suppression.
Dispatch-time enable checks arise only from the spec-introduced enablement switch.
A staged rollout with withheld access after failed verification is process beyond creating the bot.
Idempotent repeated activation arises only from the spec's activation/rollback recovery lifecycle.
Last-write-wins for settings is true of any configuration store and decides nothing a builder can act on.
A single-callout bot cannot exhaust 100 callouts per transaction; the clause requires nothing actionable.
A single callout under a 30-second deadline cannot reach the 120-second cumulative limit; nothing to build.
Says only that a platform refusal is not success, which holds for any product; no builder action follows.
Restates that a Salesforce concurrency refusal is not a successful reply; true of any product, nothing to build.
Payloads bounded by 4,000 code points and 2,048 tokens cannot approach 6 MB; nothing to act on.
That a queued deployment is not complete is true of any Salesforce deployment and decides nothing.
Production deployment requirements fall outside a bot requested only for a development org.
Production coverage gates fall outside a bot requested only for a development org.
A marketplace managed-package listing is far beyond the requested development-org bot.
Describes xAI's retention policy without requiring anything of the builder.
Grant removal on rollback depends on the spec-introduced rollback capability.
Clearing provider configuration on rollback depends on the spec-introduced rollback capability.
With a 4,000-code-point input and 2,048-token ceiling the context window cannot be exceeded; nothing to act on.
Reporting incomplete rollback depends on the spec-introduced rollback capability.
Credential status semantics arise only from the spec-introduced configuration inspection view.
Blocking held attempts across reinstallation depends on rollback and attempt-validity machinery the spec introduced.
